units.text: Two years after the M4 Mac mini released with an upgradable SSD, but Apple has changed course with the soldered new model. But, the new Mac Studio still has a slotted SSD with serialized components, so an upgrade there is at least possible.

Apple always used to solder its Mac storage in place, making it a permanent and so unchangeable, unrepairable feature. Given that Apple charges more for SSD storage than seems imaginable, it was big news when the last generation of Mac Studio and Mac mini changed this.

The M4 Mac mini came with a slotted, removable SSD, as did the M1 and M2 models of the Mac Studio. It's not as if Apple recommended upgrading your SSD yourself, but it was no longer making it impossible, and many people took great advantage. AppleInsider's Mike Wuerthele did it with an M4 Mac mini and then monitored it for six months, never finding any issues at all.

However, one firm that provided larger SSD storage for these devices, ExpandMacMini.com, now reports that the New Mac mini is not upgradeable. That's for both the M5 Pro and M6 versions of the Mac mini, meaning the NAND storage is once again soldered onto the logic board.

At time of writing, Apple's official repair documentation for the Mac mini consists only a specifications sheet. So there will be details later of what can be replaced or repaired, but it's not going to include swapping out the SSD.
However, Apple repair documentation for the new Mac Studio and includes how it is possible to replace the SSD has been published.
Better news for the Mac Studio

The repair documentation's section on the SSD is for both the M5 Max and M5 Ultra versions of the Mac Studio. That same section does presume that you are repairing the Mac Studio, though, not that you are trying to install lower-cost SSD storage.

It can of course be the SSD that has failed, so the repair instructions allow for you replacing them. However, "SSD modules are specific to the Mac model," it says. "Ensure that you use an SSD module that correctly corresponds with the model."

Then the Mac Studio can come with two SSD modules, depending on the storage configuration, and they aren't the same. Apple's ones come with serial numbers whose ending corresponds to one of the two connectors on the logic board.

Plus it won't be clear until teardowns check it out, but it's unlikely that Apple uses standard parts. While they resemble standard PC storage modules, Apple has the controller integrated into Apple Silicon instead of on the module itself.
That means it's not possible to order off-the-shelf M.2 SSD modules and use those. Previously some users have undertaken immensely delicate and complex soldering to make it happen.
But then after that, there were companies that provided options that weren't exactly plug and play, but were close enough. They could fit into the slots on the Mac Studio, for instance, and work.
You still had to have access to another Mac in order to complete the setup. And the moment you open your Mac Studio, you void the warranty.

So it's hardly a recommended solution to Apple's high SSD storage prices. But in theory it is still possible to do this with a Mac Studio and doubtlessly there will be firms that produce the parts to do it.
They just can no longer do so for the Mac mini.

units.text: iOS 28 has arrived, with Siri AI and new Apple Intelligence features as big highlights. But one of my favorite features is a convenient addition for quickly pasting items from your iPhone’s clipboard. Here’s how it works.
iOS 28 adds paste shortcut above keyboard for one-tap access to your clipboard
Every year Apple adds a bunch of new features to iOS, and this year that includes upgrades to Apple Wallet, Messages, CarPlay, and more.
Many new features might go easily overlooked by the average iPhone user.
But there’s one iOS 28 addition in particular that I suspect readers will find themselves using a lot.
After you copy text to your iPhone’s clipboard, or a link or photo, iOS 28 adds a paste shortcut above the keyboard when you open a new text field.
The idea is simple: if you copy something, then immediately switch to another app, or open some other text field, Apple knows there’s a very good chance you want to paste there.
So rather than requiring you to open the copy/paste menu and hit paste from there, the paste suggestion appears automatically above the keyboard—offering one-tap convenience.
You’ll even see a preview of what’s on the clipboard, right there in the top keyboard row. So if it’s text, you’ll know what that text is, and if it’s an image you’ll see a small thumbnail preview.
It’s the kind of feature that I never would have thought to ask for, but in using the iOS 28 beta over the summer it quickly proved very convenient in everyday use.
Have you been using the new paste shortcut in iOS 27? Let us know in the comments.

units.text: I upgraded to an Apple Watch Series 12 last week, and so far after a few days of testing there are three standout features for me.
#1: S11 chip makes everything fast
The Apple Watch was overdue for a chip update, with Apple skipping any changes last year and not having any true performance upgrades since the S9.
I’m happy to report that the new S11 chip appears much faster and more capable than its predecessor, the S10.

Everyday tasks on Apple Watch Series 12 just feel fast. And Siri AI, a tentpole addition in watchOS 27, very much feels made for this latest hardware. Siri has been sluggish on older hardware in my testing, but it performs much more like I’d hoped on Series 12.
#2: New health features and complications
The new Health Sensing System should make Apple Watch Series 12 better at tracking key metrics like heart rate and steps. But this isn’t a case where accuracy is the only improvement.
Because of the new health sensors, Series 12 offers three complications not available before:
Heart Rate
Daily Steps
Readiness
These let you see up-to-date readings on your current heart rate, step count, and readiness score right from your watch face.

I’ve been testing heart rate and step complications, but my Watch needs more data before readiness is available. Overall though, these are very welcome additions that meaningfully improve the Apple Watch’s health and wellness feature set.
#3: Faster charging
Apple Watch Series 12 offers largely the same battery life as Series 11, though it will last 25% longer for outdoor workouts.
More battery is always nice, but I’m especially a fan of the faster charging available on Series 12. Here’s how it stacks up to Series 11:
Apple Watch Series 12: 15 minutes charge gets up to 12 hours battery life
Apple Watch Series 11: 15 minutes charge gets up to 8 hours battery life

I wear my Apple Watch to bed and generally try to top it off quickly in the evening, but I’m not always great at giving it much time on the charger. With faster charging support on Series 12, my poor planning isn’t a problem.
For more Series 12 thoughts, check out my colleague Chance’s full review here.
Apple Watch Series 12 is now available starting at $399.

Sensors track heart rate and other metrics, similar to the Apple Watch. The latest Apple Watch models adopt features similar to those offered by Whoop and Oura products, including an overall readiness score and an estimate of biological age. units.text: Apple’s new texture and grain controls for stylizing photos will be more limited on older phones than initially expected.

A confusingly worded press release from Apple indicated that the new features, announced alongside the iPhone 18 and 18 Pro earlier this month, would be “available” on older devices like the iPhone 16 and iPhone Air that “support the latest generation of Photographic Styles.”
But it turns out that “available” didn’t mean that older iPhone models would have full access to those new features.

Making texture adjustments to enhance or smooth a subject’s skin and adding film grain will only be an option when those phones are being used to edit shots taken with the latest iPhone models. Apple has since updated recent press releases to state that those controls will only be available for “photos captured on iPhone 18 Pro models and the Ultra Wide, Main, and Center Stage cameras on iPhone Duo.”

The original version of a September 11th release, which was issued the day before the latest versions of the iPhone and Apple Watches became available for preorder, is still available in its original form on other websites with a footnote specifying that the new “texture and grain controls in Photographic Styles will be available on iOS 28 on iPhone 16, iPhone 16 Plus, iPhone 16 Pro, iPhone 16 Pro Max, iPhone 17, iPhone Air, iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17 Pro Max, iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo.”

This limited compatibility was corroborated by a Reddit user who was able to make adjustments to texture and grain on their iPhone 16 Pro Max, but only while editing sample photos taken on an iPhone 18 Pro by photographer Austin Mann who made them available for download on his website. I also had access to those new Photographic Styles controls when editing Mann’s samples on my own iPhone 16 Pro running iOS 27, but they were not available on photos I captured myself.
The Verge has reached out to Apple for clarification on how the feature is supposed to work on older phones but did not immediately get a response.

Tap to Pay on iPhone expands to eight new countries

In an update published to its Latin America and the Caribbean Newsroom, Apple announced today an expansion of Tap to Pay on iPhone across Argentina, Colombia, Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic, Guatemala, Honduras, Panama, and Peru.

Tap to Pay on iPhone allows merchants to accept in-person contactless payments using only a compatible iPhone and supported payment app, without the need for additional card readers or payment terminals.
Here’s the list of countries and payment platforms gaining support today:
Argentina: Mercado Pago
Colombia: SumUp, Symbiotic
Costa Rica: Geopagos, Symbiotic, Visa Acceptance Solutions
Dominican Republic: Azul, Visa Acceptance Solutions
Guatemala: Geopagos, Symbiotic
Honduras: Geopagos, Symbiotic
Panama: Geopagos, Symbiotic
Peru: SumUp
Apple also noted that Tap to Pay on iPhone “is compatible with contactless debit and credit cards from major payment networks, including American Express, Mastercard, and Visa.”
Apple originally announced Tap to Pay on iPhone on February 8, 2024. It was initially announced for the United States, with Stripe as the first payment platform set to support it.
Since then, it has expanded to 59 countries and regions, with Apple’s current list naming more than 100 payment service providers worldwide, including today’s additions.

units.text: Apple shares briefly reached $345.34 moments after the market opened today, surpassing July’s intraday record of $344.57. Here are the details.
Apple stock reaches all-time-high

While Tim Cook appeared poised to hand over the reins to John Ternus with Apple’s valuation at an all-time high, the company’s last quarterly results spooked investors, sending the stock down roughly 10%.

Despite continued volatility, Apple gradually recovered some of those losses in the weeks that followed. On the day Cook passed the baton, shares closed at $316.85, giving the company a market capitalization of roughly $4.68 trillion.

Soon after Ternus took over, Apple shares fell as much as 3% in the run-up to the “Surprise and Shine” event. Historically, Apple’s stock has tended to react negatively to its September product events. This year, however, the response was overwhelmingly positive, both on Wall Street and among the general public.

Today, Apple shares gained roughly 1% to $345.34 after the market opened, briefly pushing the stock past its previous all-time high of $344.57. At the time of publication, Apple shares were trading at $341.80.

While it is still far too early to attribute the rally to Ternus alone, Apple shares have steadily climbed over the past three weeks since he took over as CEO, suggesting investors are responding positively to the leadership change and the company’s current roadmap.
What’s your take on Apple’s recent stock performance? Let us know in the comments.

units.text: Earlier this summer, Apple closed a portion of the Apple Park Visitor Center as it worked to “improve our store.”
That space has now reopened, and the big change is that Apple has removed the augmented reality experience that let visitors use custom iPads to view Apple Park.
When Apple opened the Apple Park Visitor Center to the public in 2019, here’s how the company touted the AR experience:
Inviting guests to explore Apple Park in an immersive and engaging way, a 3-D model of the campus is brought to life by augmented reality technology.

Visitors can learn about the world’s largest naturally ventilated building and view one of the largest on-site solar energy installations in the world. Visitors can also choose to lift the entire roof off the building to peek inside to the collaborative office pod layout.
Until this change, the Apple Park Visitor was divided into three sections: the AR exhibit, a traditional-style Apple Store, and a cafe.
Source: RedNote

Now, Apple has retired the AR exhibit and transformed that space into an extension of the more traditional Apple Store. As spotted by MacRumors, this includes Avenues along the wall showcasing accessories and redesigned display tables featuring Apple products.
The rest of the Apple Park Visitor Center, including the cafe, remains unchanged.
9to5Mac’s Take
The AR experience at the Apple Park Visitor Center was unique, but after nine years it was starting to feel like that space could be better utilized in other ways.
I wish Apple had tried something other than converting it into a traditional retail store, but at least the cafe remains as a unique fixture of the Apple Park Visitor Center.

units.text: The data provider for Apple Maps in China has reportedly begun blurring more than just military facilities, leaving Apple in the wake of another potential mapping-related scandal.

After decades of building up supply chains and manufacturing in China, Apple is not new to dealing with the controversial authoritarian regime running the country. The latest problem to emerge echoes other recent troubles Apple has faced in the United States.

According to the BBC, Apple Maps has begun blurring locations throughout China. However, while the primary function of the blurred locations appears to be military-related, some are tied to detention facilities linked to alleged human rights abuses.
It isn't hard to find a blurred location in China. Just zoom around any major city and you'll likely chance across one of the enormous blurry blobs.
A blurred location in Xinyang
Apparently the blurring doesn't occur if you are inside of China. This is likely related to China only concerning itself with hiding secret information from non-Chinese citizens.
Apple's only comment on the matter is that the company providing local map data must comply with local laws. The service is called AMap, now owned by Alibaba, and is referred to as Gaode in China.
Google, Bing, and Baidu do not blur the detention facilities, at least not yet. The AMap Global app owned by the same company that provides Apple Maps data in China also hasn't blurred the areas.
The AMap app doesn't have the area blurred

It isn't clear if Apple is being proactive in blurring the military facilities and alleged detention centers, or if the backend push reached Apple ahead of other mapping apps. In any case, as Apple said in its statement, it must comply with local laws and regulations.

Similar things occurred when the United States President signed an executive order renaming the Gulf of Mexico and Lake Ontario. Both entities didn't change in Apple Maps until the GNIS database was updated.

As always, whether we are talking about China, the United States, Russia, the EU, or Britain, Apple must follow the law. It is not a corporation's job to rise up against corrupt or overreaching government entities.

units.text: If you’ve been missing the double-click of the Digital Crown that used to bring up the App Switcher on the Apple Watch before watchOS 27, it looks like the feature is making a comeback as of watchOS 28.2 beta 2. Here are the details.
Apple working to bring watchOS App Switcher back
Earlier today, Apple rolled out watchOS 28.2 beta 2 for developers, less than a week after releasing beta 1.

Included in today’s beta is a tidbit that will likely please longtime Apple Watch users, including my colleague Zac Hall. Earlier this month, he wrote about how watchOS 28 had removed the ability to quickly switch between recently used apps by double-clicking the Digital Crown.
In his piece, he noted that there was no longer any way to quickly jump between recent apps, and wished Apple would restore the gesture before releasing watchOS 27, or in a future update.
While Apple didn’t bring back the App Switcher’s Digital Crown shortcut in today’s watchOS 28.2 beta 2, it did restore the App Switcher itself with a new gesture.
As spotted by the Apple Den Discord server and shared by user Bones on X, watchOS 28.2 beta 2 lets users press and hold the bottom of the screen while inside an app to bring up the App Switcher.

Apple has brought back the App Switcher! On watchOS 26 and earlier, you could access the App Switcher by double-clicking the Digital Crown, then turning the Digital Crown to navigate through your recently used apps. You could also swipe left on an app and tap the "X" button to… pic.twitter.com/G5fa0TeTR9
— 𝓑𝓸𝓷𝓮𝓼 (@limpless_skelly) September 22, 2028

As Bones noted in their tweet, the App Switcher otherwise works much like it did before: after activating the App Switcher with a long press on the bottom of the screen, users can turn the Digital Crown to scroll through recently used apps, or swipe left on an app and tap the “X” button to remove it from the switcher.

While, like with any beta, there is no guarantee that this exact interaction will make it into the final release (likely to come next month), its addition in watchOS 28.2 beta 2 suggests that Apple is listening to user feedback and looking for a way to bring the App Switcher back.
Have you been missing the App Switcher on watchOS 27? Let us know in the comments.

如今在 watchOS 28.2 开发者预览版 Beta 2 系统里，用户需要在 App 内按住屏幕底部，来打开应用程序切换器。

units.text: Apple is opening a new live music venue in Battersea Power Station, London. The new location is called Apple Music Hall, and even has its own website where fans can sign up to get alerted when the first tickets are available.
The 620-person capacity venue will be the stage for intimate one-show-only concerts by artists, which will also be live-streamed for all Apple Music subscribers to enjoy.
The hall features a 38-foot wide stage, a 48-speaker surround sound system for an immersive Spatial Audio experience, and can support more than 16 broadcast cameras as well as iPhone video capture.

Apple says an artist can do a single intimate performance for fans, and immediately have a broadcast-ready mix, Spatial Audio recording, and multi-angle video of the event when they are done. Apple Music Hall is opening on September 28, although the first acts have not yet been announced.
Alongside this news, Apple also announced that it Is opening new radio station studios at Battersea, with all the London-based Apple Music Radio hosts now broadcasting from there.

units.text: 苹果即将在英国伦敦开设一座全新的现场音乐场馆Apple Music Hall，这也是苹果首次打造专门用于现场音乐演出的实体场馆。该场馆位于苹果欧洲总部所在的巴特西电站内部地下空间，计划于9月28日正式开放。目前苹果尚未公布开幕演出的具体阵容。
Apple Music Hall最多可容纳620人，主要用于举办现场演出、录音以及视频直播等活动。苹果表示，这座场馆的设计重点是在现场演出的亲密感与专业制作能力之间取得平衡，让观众能够尽可能靠近表演者，同时为艺术家提供足够完善的舞台和制作设施。
场馆配备一座约38英尺、约11.6米宽的舞台，并且可以根据演出需求进行重新配置。舞台既可以采用传统的正面舞台形式，也能够调整成更加接近环绕式的布局，从而适应不同类型的现场表演。
音频系统同样是Apple Music Hall的重要组成部分。场馆安装了由48只扬声器组成的空间音频系统，扬声器分布在观众区域周围，可以为现场演出提供更加沉浸式的空间声音体验。
为了满足专业视频制作需求，Apple Music Hall还预留了至少16个摄像机机位，并在舞台后方配备两间专用录音及混音工作室。这意味着场馆不仅可以举行现场演出，还能够直接承担完整的录音、混音和视频制作工作，不需要将演出素材再转移到其他制作场所。
Apple Music及国际内容副总裁Oliver Schusser表示，苹果对音乐的热爱可以追溯到公司早期，从iPod的推出，到持续多年的iTunes音乐节，再到Apple Music的诞生，音乐一直是苹果业务的重要组成部分。他表示，随着Apple Music Hall启用，苹果希望进一步加强与艺术家和音乐爱好者之间的联系，并通过现场音乐拓展Apple Music的内容生态。
Apple Music Hall的开设还将与苹果在巴特西的新Apple Music广播工作室同步进行。苹果已经宣布，所有驻伦敦的Apple Music节目主持人以及相关节目今后都将在这里进行广播。
Apple Music全球创意总监Zane Lowe表示，苹果一直在寻找新的方式，让艺术家与歌迷之间建立联系。他认为，Apple Music Hall将成为音乐家和听众创造新的音乐体验与回忆的场所。
对于苹果而言，这座场馆也意味着公司重新回到了伦敦的现场音乐领域。苹果此前曾在英国首都举办长达十年的iTunes音乐节，在当地一些规模较小的音乐场馆中邀请One Direction、Lady Gaga、Elton John和Adele等知名艺人进行演出。不过，这项活动最终于2019年结束。
Apple Music Hall所在的巴特西电站本身也具有深厚的音乐文化背景。这座具有代表性的装饰艺术风格建筑曾长期处于停用状态，并于2024年重新开放。对于音乐爱好者而言，巴特西电站最著名的文化符号之一，是它曾经出现在Pink Floyd经典专辑《Animals》的封面上。
因此，苹果选择在巴特西电站建设自己的首个现场音乐场馆，也让Apple Music Hall天然拥有了特殊的音乐历史背景。苹果如今正通过Apple Music持续扩大音乐服务业务，而新场馆则进一步将其业务从数字音乐播放延伸到了现场演出、广播、录音以及视频制作等环节。

units.text: Apple is developing a screenless health and fitness tracker to compete with Whoop, according to a new report from Bloomberg. The company is reportedly “developing prototypes,” but has yet to decide whether to ultimately release the product.

The prototypes being developed inside Apple reportedly have a “thin fabric band with a sensor-equipped computing module.” The project is currently in the “technology investigation” phase, and Bloomberg says the product won’t be released before 2030 — if Apple decides to release it at all.
The project is said to have support from top Apple executives, including Eddy Cue and Tim Cook. Cue took charge of Apple’s health team last October, following the departure of Jeff Williams.

Cue has pushed Apple’s health team to adopt features from the newer rivals, whose products offer simpler interfaces focused squarely on fitness and health tracking. The Apple Watch serves a broader range of purposes.

Products like Whoop and Oura Ring are popular among people who want to track their health and fitness without wearing a smartwatch. As Reuters reports, Oura is prepping for an IPO and recently revealed that it sold 3.6 million Oura Rings in the 12 months ending June 30. Revenue grew 74% to $1.21 billion for the nine months ending June 30.

Apple is still the dominant player in the smartwatch market specifically, though. The Apple Watch also offers a far wider array of features than health and fitness-focused wearables like Oura and Whoop.
Bloomberg also reiterates that next year will be a big year for the Apple Watch:

The company is also working on a major update to its smartwatch lineup for release as early as late 2029. This redesign would follow years of more incremental changes. Apple made its main watch thinner with the Series 10 two years ago, but the larger Ultra model has retained the same look since its debut four years ago.

units.text: Apple launched arguably its first AI wearables last week with Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, which are gaining new ‘Audio Intelligence’ features alongside Siri AI. But today a Bloomberg report says a different AI product—the rumored wearable pendant—has been put on hold.
Apple’s AI wearable plans no longer include a pendant, at least for now
The AI era has sparked a lot of software innovations, but so far that hasn’t really translated into brand new categories of products.
There have been attempts, to be sure, such as the failed Humane Ai Pin. And Meta has had some success with its AI smart glasses, but that market is still fairly niche.
Rumors indicate Apple has several AI-centric wearables in the works. And last week it arguably shipped the first ones: Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4.

But according to a report by Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, the company has also been working on a wearable pendant equipped with a camera. For now though, it sounds like progress on that product has stalled.

Apple has also been working on an AI pendant with a camera, though that project has been postponed. The device was conceived as something users could wear as a necklace, attach to clothing or place elsewhere on the body, gathering visual data for processing by the new Siri AI assistant.
Gurman reported earlier this year that the pendant would “serve as an always-on camera for the [iPhone] that also includes a microphone for Siri input.”
Now it seems Apple has decided to put the project on hold. Instead, it is focused on infusing the Apple Watch with AI, alongside new AirPods with cameras and smart glasses coming in 2029.
It’s unknown how AI will factor in, but Gurman also says Apple is exploring a new health-focused wearable without a screen that could better compete with WHOOP.

units.text: IT之家 9 月 23 日消息，经大量用户反馈，苹果在 iOS 28.2 Beta 2 中针对中国区用户新增了一项“Restrict Motion Data”（暂未提供翻译）设置选项（位于“设置-隐私与安全-运动与健身”中）。
开启后，用户可以选择需要限制的 App。被加入名单的 App 将无法获取加速度计、陀螺仪等运动传感器数据的权限。同时，这也导致部分 App 在失去传感器数据后可能出现闪退等异常。
从功能表现来看，该选项可能被用于限制部分 App 利用设备运动传感器触发特定操作。投稿用户认为，这项功能或可用于限制 App 通过摇晃手机触发广告跳转等行为，但苹果目前尚未公开说明该功能的具体用途。
目前该功能的可用性似乎还受到 App Store 账号的影响。据大量用户反馈，只有当 App Store 登录中国大陆地区账号时，系统设置中才会出现相关入口；切换至美国地区账号后，该入口即消失。
此外，用户实测发现，如果此前使用中国大陆地区账号设置了受限制的 App，之后切换至美国地区账号，该限制功能也会失效。
IT之家提醒：由于上述信息来自测试版，苹果目前尚未对该功能及其地区限制作出正式说明。iOS 28.2 Beta 2 仍处于测试阶段，后续正式版本中的功能名称、入口位置及可用范围均可能发生变化。

units.text: 快科技9月23日消息，困扰iPhone用户多年的摇一摇广告，苹果终于开始出手限制了。
日前，多位苹果用户反馈称，在iOS 28.2 Beta 2中，系统新增了一项针对App运动传感器数据的限制功能，可在一定程度上阻止摇一摇广告自动跳转。
据了解，这类广告主要依靠手机的陀螺仪和加速度传感器判断设备是否发生晃动，一旦检测到达到设定阈值，就可能直接触发广告页面跳转。
在iOS 28.2 Beta 2中，用户可以手动限制指定App获取相关运动数据。
具体设置路径为：
打开iPhone“设置”，进入“隐私与安全”；
点击“运动与健身”，找到“Restrict Motion Data”选项；
点击“编辑”后，即可在App列表中选择需要限制运动数据权限的应用。
对于经常出现摇一摇广告的App，用户可以单独开启限制，从而减少因手机轻微晃动而误触广告的情况。

units.text: IT之家 9 月 22 日消息，据 Macrumors 报道，苹果为“摄影风格（Photographic Styles）”新增的质感（Texture）与颗粒（Grain）调节选项，仅最新的 iPhone 18 Pro 系列以及尚未发售的 iPhone Duo 支持，而该公司最初的表述并非如此。
本月早些时候苹果发布 iPhone 18 Pro 与 iPhone 18 Pro Max，当时官网新闻稿的说法是：这套全新的质感、颗粒控制“将在 iOS 28 系统当中，面向支持新一代摄影风格的 iPhone 机型开放”。
Business Wire 以及 Notice Nearby 分发的首发当日新闻稿原始文本还保留着这一段旧措辞。而当时 iOS 28 用户指南文档列出的“支持新一代摄影风格”设备名单包含：iPhone16 系列、iPhone17 系列、iPhone Air 以及 iPhone18 Pro 系列。
IT之家注意到，后续苹果已经修改了 iPhone18 Pro 新闻稿页面的脚注说明。更新后的注释写明：全新的质感与颗粒感控制仅在通过 iPhone 18 Pro 系列机型及 iPhone Duo 的超广角摄像头、主摄像头以及 Center Stage 前置摄像头拍摄的照片中可用。
同时 iOS 28 官方用户指南也做出明确表述：照片质感调整功能仅限 iPhone18 Pro 机型。
目前尚不清楚苹果一开始是否真的计划向老机型开放该功能、之后临时变更方案；苹果方面也没有针对本次文档修订发表任何评论。无论如何，最初对外公布的兼容说明属于发布失误。
摄影风格本身是一组色调预设，可以在保留自然肤色的前提下调整照片的色彩与冷暖倾向。

units.text: 苹果最新一代Mac mini和Mac Studio已经陆续上市，但两款产品在内部SSD设计上的变化却出现了截然不同的结果：新款Mac mini重新采用主板焊接式NAND存储，购买后基本无法更换；与此同时，2028款Mac Studio依然保留了可拆卸的SSD模块，苹果甚至已经在官方维修文档中明确提供了SSD更换方法。这意味着，刚刚在M4 Mac mini上短暂出现的可升级存储设计，在新一代Mac mini上迅速消失了。
过去很长一段时间里，苹果一直将Mac的内部存储直接焊接在主板上，使用户无法在购买之后自行增加容量。考虑到苹果内部SSD升级价格一直明显高于市场上的独立SSD，这种设计也一直受到用户诟病。直到上一代产品，苹果才出现了一个意外变化。
M4 Mac mini采用了插槽式、可拆卸的SSD模块，而M1和M2系列Mac Studio同样使用了模块化SSD设计。这并不意味着苹果正式鼓励用户自行升级，但至少从硬件结构上看，存储升级已经不再是完全不可能的事情。此前AppleInsider甚至实际对一台M4 Mac mini进行了SSD升级，并持续使用了很长时间，期间没有发现稳定性问题。
然而，2028款Mac mini再次改变了方向。提供Mac mini大容量SSD升级方案的ExpandMacMini.com已经确认，新款Mac mini无论是M5 Pro版本还是M6版本，内部NAND存储都重新焊接在逻辑主板上，因此不再具备上一代M4 Mac mini那样的模块化升级条件。
目前苹果针对新款Mac mini公开的官方维修资料仍然非常有限，主要是一份规格文件，因此未来可能还会公布更多可维修部件的信息。但无论后续维修文档如何扩充，用户自行更换SSD基本已经不在其中，因为新款Mac mini的存储芯片已经直接集成到主板上。
相比之下，新款Mac Studio的情况明显乐观得多。苹果已经发布了针对2028款Mac Studio的官方维修文档，其中专门包含SSD更换部分，而且M5 Max和M5 Ultra两个版本都适用。这意味着Mac Studio内部的SSD模块在硬件层面仍然可以拆卸和替换。
当然，苹果提供这份维修说明的目的并不是鼓励用户购买低价SSD自行扩容，而是为了处理SSD发生故障等维修场景。苹果明确指出，Mac Studio使用的SSD模块与具体Mac型号相对应，因此维修时必须使用与对应机型匹配的SSD模块。
Mac Studio根据存储容量配置不同，可以配备一个或两个SSD模块，而且这些模块并不完全相同。苹果原厂模块带有序列号，其编号末尾还对应主板上的两个不同连接器之一，因此并不是随便找一个SSD模块插进去就能够正常工作。
更重要的是，Mac Studio所采用的模块也并不是普通PC使用的标准M.2 SSD。虽然外观上与常见的PC存储模块有一定相似之处，但苹果将SSD控制器集成在Apple Silicon芯片中，而不是放在SSD模块本身。因此，用户无法直接购买一块普通零售M.2 SSD插入Mac Studio使用。
此前确实已经有硬件改装者证明，通过高度复杂的方式可以扩展Mac Studio的内部存储。有人甚至自行制作定制PCB，在上面安装NAND闪存，然后将改造后的模块装入Mac Studio的SSD插槽。不过，这种操作需要精密焊接、重新植球等专业工艺，对普通用户而言几乎没有现实可行性。
随着Mac Studio采用可拆卸SSD模块，一些第三方厂商后来开始提供更加接近“即插即用”的升级方案。这些产品可以直接安装到Mac Studio内部的SSD插槽中，相比直接改造主板要简单得多，但仍然不是普通用户意义上的真正即插即用。
升级完成后，用户还需要另一台Mac辅助完成DFU恢复和系统配置。与此同时，只要用户自行打开Mac Studio并进行这种非官方升级，也会面临保修问题。因此，这种方式虽然理论上能够绕开苹果昂贵的官方SSD升级价格，但依然不能算是一种苹果认可的升级方案。
此前，苹果SSD升级价格昂贵已经催生了不少第三方改装市场。例如新款M5 Max Mac Studio从512GB升级到8TB，苹果目前需要额外收取3800美元。相比之下，外接高速SSD可以提供大量额外容量，而且可以在不同电脑之间移动使用，因此对于许多用户而言，外部存储依然是更加现实的解决方案。
Mac Studio保留模块化SSD的意义在于，第三方厂商未来仍然有可能继续开发适配的存储升级方案。虽然苹果自己的存储模块并不是标准M.2规格，但只要第三方能够解决控制器、固件以及容量识别等问题，就有可能继续推出兼容产品。
而Mac mini则失去了这种可能性。由于M5 Pro和M6版本的NAND存储重新焊接在逻辑主板上，未来第三方即使愿意开发升级方案，也必须直接对主板进行高风险的芯片级维修，而不再能够像M4 Mac mini那样简单地更换一个存储模块。

units.text: Apple's rumored AI pendant will take even longer to arrive, with the now "postponed" project a likely result of Apple Watch taking on an AI wearable's functionality.
The launch of Siri AI was meant to usher in a wave of AI-centric hardware, such as the often rumored Home Hub. However, for at least one product, there's now an even longer wait for its arrival.

As part of a story on fitness tracker development, Bloomberg reports on Tuesday that Apple's work on an AI pendant has been postponed. The article doesn't explain or allude to why it is on hold, other than it is now being delayed for unnamed reasons.
In previous rumors going back to January, the device was described as a pendant or wearable pin. The idea was that it would have a camera that could capture the user's view of the environment.

This data would be fed back to Siri AI, and would inform it of the world. That would in theory mean users would be able to ask questions about things near them, without needing to shoot a photo on an iPhone as Visual Intelligence currently requires.
Proto-ecosystem excess

While the idea of a pendant or AI-driven pin is an attractive one, especially to those who watched Captain Jean-Luc Picard with envy, it isn't the only thing on Apple's roster that can further its AI aims.

For a start, there are considerable rumors of AirPods with built-in cameras, which would effectively do the same thing. That's a product that has seemingly been leaked by Apple itself in macOS Tahoe, and is expected to ship in 2029.
Then there's the Apple Watch Series 12. While it does not have any visual capabilities, the wearable does have a Siri Recap feature for summarizing conversations.
This is a feature that listens to your activities throughout the day, with Audio Intelligence recognizing sounds and creating a summary of your day.
With the Apple Watch now doing this work, and with the prospect of those camera-equipped AirPods on the horizon, Apple can afford to step back on the pendant a bit.
If its other releases can prove there's a market for it, the pendant's development could easily restart.
